\chapter{Fifth Return: The Core Verbs}
\label{ch:gu-core-verb-fifth-return}
\hlchaptermodality{30}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can still recognise and write the numbers and core verbs I met a hundred lessons ago.}

Eight zero-new-atom lessons place the numbers and the fifteen core verbs 98 to 104 positions after their introductions, scoring recognition and model-free writing separately in each.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[Practice]{ek be traṇ chār pā̃ch returns at R4}

\label{lesson:GU-R26-numbers-r4}



\begin{quote}
Before anything is uncovered: count from one to five in Gujarati.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
This lesson sits 104 positions after the material it asks for, which is inside the fourth spacing window rather than near it. Nothing new is taught here.

\subsection*{Writing — from sound, every model covered}
Score recognition and writing separately; each needs full marks on its own.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Why does Gujarati \emph{be} start with a \textbf{b} where Sanskrit had \emph{dve}, and what happened to the \textbf{r} of \emph{traṇ}? (The \textbf{dv-} cluster collapsed to \textbf{bb-} and then \textbf{b-}; the \textbf{r} was restored later by learned borrowing, not inherited.)
\end{tcolorbox}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Two rules hide in this row. Why is \emph{karvī} not \emph{karvũ}, and who is the subject of \emph{gamvũ}? (The ending agrees with the \textbf{feminine} \emph{madad}; and \emph{gamvũ} \textbf{will not take you as its subject} — the thing liked is.)
\end{tcolorbox}
